name: pdk-sid-scim-incremental-provisioning
instr:
SCIM is our source of truth for employees, but the IdServer pull skips users past the first page and never learns about deletes. An offboarded user can remain in IdServer. This affects the SCIM server and IdServer provisioning for the default realm; leave LDAP and the admin website out of scope.

To close this out:
- Add an authenticated SCIM `GET /Changes?since=<cursor>&count=<page-size>` feed for `User` and `Group` writes. Return `next` and ordered `changes` containing `sequence`, `realm`, `resourceType`, `id`, and `deleted`; include tombstones and membership changes. A cursor may advance only past committed changes, even if an earlier transaction commits after a later one. A SCIM write blocked on one resource must not stall writes to other resources, and a provisioning run started meanwhile still succeeds. `since=0` starts at the beginning; repeated reads and pagination never skip a committed change.
- Add `POST /provisioning/{id}/incremental` on IdServer, where `{id}` is the id of the default realm's existing SCIM identity provisioning (the seeded instance named `SCIM`); callers send no IdServer access token. A successful run imports the SCIM feed for the default realm and returns the durable progress as `sequence`: the feed position of the last change it applied. The first run converges for at least 2,500 users, including groups and memberships. Subsequent runs reflect creates, updates, group membership changes, deletes, deactivation and delete-then-recreate under the sa
